## Suspicious Activity Reporting (SAR)  
### When to File a SAR  
**Mandatory SAR Filing Triggers:**
- Money laundering suspected (any amount)
- Terrorist financing suspected
- Proceeds of crime (POCA) suspected
- Sanctions violation
- Large cash transactions with no obvious purpose
- Customers unwilling to provide information
- Structuring detected (deliberately avoiding reporting thresholds)  
**Discretionary SAR:**
- Unusual transaction patterns not clearly illegal
- Potential fraud (separate from AML fraud)
- Regulatory concern

raw_entities.name: Suspicious Activity Reporting Policy
raw_entities.description: Policy governing the identification, assessment, and filing of Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) to relevant authorities. Establishes mandatory and discretionary SAR filing triggers based on detection of money laundering, terrorist financing, proceeds of crime, sanctions violations, and other financial crime indicators.

raw_entities.name: Mandatory SAR Filing on Money Laundering Suspicion
raw_entities.description: Requires filing of a SAR whenever money laundering is suspected, regardless of transaction amount. This is a mandatory trigger with no discretionary threshold.

raw_entities.name: Mandatory SAR Filing on Terrorist Financing Suspicion
raw_entities.description: Requires filing of a SAR whenever terrorist financing is suspected. This is a mandatory trigger under the policy.

raw_entities.name: Mandatory SAR Filing on Proceeds of Crime Suspicion
raw_entities.description: Requires filing of a SAR when proceeds of crime under the Proceeds of Crime Act (POCA) are suspected. This is a mandatory trigger.

raw_entities.name: Mandatory SAR Filing on Sanctions Violation
raw_entities.description: Requires filing of a SAR when a sanctions violation is suspected or detected. This is a mandatory trigger.

raw_entities.name: Mandatory SAR Filing on Large Cash Transactions Without Clear Purpose
raw_entities.description: Requires filing of a SAR when large cash transactions occur with no obvious legitimate purpose. This is a mandatory trigger.
context: Large cash transactions with no obvious purpose

raw_entities.name: Mandatory SAR Filing When Customer Refuses Information Provision
raw_entities.description: Requires filing of a SAR when customers are unwilling or refuse to provide requested information. This is a mandatory trigger.

raw_entities.name: Mandatory SAR Filing on Detection of Structuring
raw_entities.description: Requires filing of a SAR when structuring is detected — the deliberate practice of breaking up transactions to avoid reporting thresholds. This is a mandatory trigger.

raw_entities.name: Discretionary SAR Filing on Unusual Transaction Patterns
raw_entities.description: Permits discretionary SAR filing when unusual transaction patterns are detected that are not clearly illegal. This is a discretionary trigger allowing staff judgment.
context: Unusual transaction patterns not clearly illegal

raw_entities.name: Discretionary SAR Filing on Potential Fraud
raw_entities.description: Permits discretionary SAR filing when potential fraud is suspected, distinct from AML-related fraud. This is a discretionary trigger.

raw_entities.name: Discretionary SAR Filing on Regulatory Concern
raw_entities.description: Permits discretionary SAR filing when a regulatory concern arises that warrants reporting. This is a discretionary trigger.

raw_entities.name: Money Laundering
raw_entities.description: The risk of customer funds or transactions being used to conceal the origins of illegally obtained money. Identified as a mandatory SAR filing trigger in this policy.

raw_entities.name: Terrorist Financing
raw_entities.description: The risk of the bank's services being used to finance terrorist activities or organizations. Identified as a mandatory SAR filing trigger.

raw_entities.name: Proceeds of Crime
raw_entities.description: The risk of handling or facilitating the movement of proceeds derived from criminal activity under the Proceeds of Crime Act. Identified as a mandatory SAR filing trigger.

raw_entities.name: Sanctions Violation
raw_entities.description: The risk of conducting transactions with sanctioned individuals, entities, or jurisdictions in breach of applicable sanctions regimes. Identified as a mandatory SAR filing trigger.

raw_entities.name: Transaction Structuring
raw_entities.description: The risk of customers deliberately breaking up transactions into smaller amounts to avoid triggering reporting thresholds and regulatory scrutiny. Identified as a mandatory SAR filing trigger.

raw_entities.name: Fraud
raw_entities.description: The risk of fraudulent activity on customer accounts or transactions, distinct from AML-related fraud. Identified as a discretionary SAR filing trigger.

raw_entities.name: SAR Filing Obligation
raw_entities.description: The overarching obligation to file Suspicious Activity Reports to the relevant authority when mandatory or discretionary triggers are met. Covers both mandatory and discretionary filing scenarios.

properties.core_policy_statement: The bank must file Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) when money laundering, terrorist financing, proceeds of crime, sanctions violations, structuring, or other financial crimes are suspected.
properties.scope_summary: Applies to all transactions and customer activities where mandatory or discretionary SAR filing triggers are identified.

properties.risk_definition: Suspected conversion or transfer of proceeds from criminal activity to conceal their origin
Suspected provision or collection of funds intended to support terrorist activities or organizations
Suspected funds derived from criminal activity as defined under the Proceeds of Crime Act
Suspected transaction or customer involvement with sanctioned jurisdictions, entities, or individuals
Deliberate fragmentation of transactions to avoid reporting thresholds or detection
examples: splitting large cash deposits into smaller amounts
multiple transactions just below reporting limits

properties.risk_definition: Suspected fraudulent activity separate from AML-related fraud

properties.filing_obligation: Mandatory when money laundering, terrorist financing, proceeds of crime, sanctions violations, structuring, or customer refusal to provide information is suspected; discretionary for unusual patterns, potential fraud, or regulatory concerns
properties.confidentiality_rule: SAR filing and related information must be kept confidential; disclosure to customer is prohibited except in limited circumstances
